([[2003 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2003]]) * 2× First-team All-[[Conference USA]] (2002, 2003) }} '''Clifton Reece Gaines''' (born January 7, 1981) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player and former assistant coach at [[Austin Spurs]]. ==High school and college career== Gaines, a {{convert|6|ft|6|in|adj=on}}, {{convert|205|lb|adj=on}} [[shooting guard]], played [[high school]] basketball at [[Madison West High School|Madison West]] in his hometown of [[Madison, Wisconsin]]. He then played four years at the [[University of Louisville]], earning [[Associated Press|AP]] All-America 3rd-team honors his senior season while leading the Cardinals to a 25–7 win–loss record. He is considered one of the best all-time shooting guards for the Louisville Cardinal basketball program. He ranks among the top-five Louisville leaders in made [[three-point field goals]] (225), [[free throws]] (456) and [[assist (basketball)|assists]] (475).{{Cite web |title=Reece Gaines Profile - Louisville Cardinals Official Athletic Site |url=http://www.gocards.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/gaines_reece01.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131218061444/http://www.gocards.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/gaines_reece01.html |archive-date=December 18, 2013 |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=gocards.com |language=en |url-status=dead }}{{Cite news |date=2013-02-09 |title=5 Best Louisville Basketball Players of the Rick Pitino Era |url=http://thekentuckyblog.com/2013/02/08/5-best-louisville-basketball-players-of-the-rick-pitino-era/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140903080531/http://thekentuckyblog.com/2013/02/08/5-best-louisville-basketball-players-of-the-rick-pitino-era/ |archive-date=September 3, 2014 |access-date=2025-07-27 |work=The Kentucky Blog |language=en-US |url-status=live }} [[Dwyane Wade]] of the [[Miami Heat]] once called Reece Gaines "the best college basketball player he ever faced".{{Cite web|url=https://www.cardchronicle.com/2012/8/29/3277365/dwyane-wade-calls-reece-gaines-the-best-college-player-he-faced|title=Dwyane Wade Calls Reece Gaines The Best College Player He Faced|first=Mike|last=Rutherford|date=August 29, 2012|website=Card Chronicle}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.wave3.com/story/19423982/gaines-happy-to-be-a-knight|title=Gaines happy to be a Knight|first=Kendrick|last=Haskins|date=August 31, 2012|website=wave3.com}} ==NBA career== Gaines was drafted by the [[Orlando Magic]] in the first round (15th overall) of the [[2003 NBA draft]] and signed with the club on July 18, 2003. He spent one season on the bench in Orlando (1.8 points, 1.0 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game in 38 games) before being traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] (along with [[Tracy McGrady]], [[Juwan Howard]] and [[Tyronn Lue]]) in exchange for [[Steve Francis]], [[Cuttino Mobley]] and [[Kelvin Cato]].{{Cite web |date=2004-06-29 |title=T-Mac finally lands in Houston |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=1831594 |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}} Gaines played ten games with the Rockets (2.6 points, 1.1 rebounds and 0.3 assists per game), spending the majority of his time on the injured list. He was traded again on February 24, 2005 (with two future second-round picks) to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] for [[Mike James (basketball, born 1975)|Mike James]] and [[Zendon Hamilton]].{{Cite web |date=2005-02-24 |others=Contributed by Marc Stein, Chad Ford & The Associated Press |title=Trade roundup: Knicks' Thomas swings two deals |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=1998814 |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} Gaines saw even less playing time with the Bucks during the second half of the [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05 season]], playing a total of 79 minutes (1.4 points, 0.3 rebounds and 0.4 assists per game) in 11 games. Gaines's playing time decreased even more with the Bucks in the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]], appearing in 12 games, and playing 52 total minutes (1.1 points, no rebounds and 0.3 assists per game). Gaines's final NBA game was played on February 12, 2006, in a 79–94 loss to the [[New Jersey Nets]] in which he recorded 2 assists and a steal. ==NBA career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===Regular season=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | align="left" | [[2003–04 NBA season|2003–04]] | align="left" | [[2003–04 Orlando Magic season|Orlando]] | '''38''' || '''1''' || 9.6 || .291 || .300 || .640 || 1.0 || '''1.1''' || '''0.3''' || '''0.1''' || 1.8 |- | align="left" | [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05]] | align="left" | [[2004–05 Houston Rockets season|Houston]] | 10 || 0 || '''10.8''' || .370 || .250 || '''.750''' || '''1.1''' || 0.3 || '''0.3''' || 0.0 || '''2.6''' |- | align="left" | [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05]] | align="left" | [[2004–05 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee]] | 11 || 0 || 7.2 || .304 || '''.500''' || .000 || 0.3 || 0.4 || 0.2 || '''0.1''' || 1.4 |- | align="left" | [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06]] | align="left" | [[2005–06 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee]] | 12 || 0 || 4.5 || '''.500''' || .000 || .250 || 0.0 || 0.3 || 0.1 || 0.0 || 1.1 |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"| Career | 71 || 1 || 8.5 || .324 || .269 || .606 || 0.7 || 0.7 || 0.2 || 0.0 || 1.7 |} ==International career== In 2006, he moved to Italy where he played for [[Angelico Biella]], [[Armani Jeans Milano]] and [[Pallacanestro Treviso|Benetton Treviso]]. In 2009, he joined the [[Bakersfield Jam]], with whom he averaged 14.3 points and 4.0 assists per game. In December 2010 he signed with [[JA Vichy]] in France.{{Cite web|url=http://javamateur2324.canalblog.com/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110112221633/http://www.ja-vichy.com/actualite-JA-Vichy-Reece-Gaines-en-renfort-a-la-JAV-137.html|url-status=dead|title=JA Vichy Basket (saison 2023/24)|archive-date=January 12, 2011|website=javamateur2324.canalblog.com}} In January 2012 Gaines signed a 30-day contract with the Fürstenfeld Panthers in Austria.{{Cite web |title=Die Panthers verstärken sich mit einem Aussenspieler |url=http://www.panthers.at/Bundesliga/News/Die-Panthers-verstaerken-sich-mit-einem-Aussenspieler |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402133151/http://www.panthers.at/Bundesliga/News/Die-Panthers-verstaerken-sich-mit-einem-Aussenspieler |archive-date=April 2, 2015 |language=de}} On February 2, 2012, the Panthers announced that the contract with Gaines would not be extended.{{Cite web|url=http://www.panthers.at/Bundesliga/News/Kaderveraenderungen-bei-den-Panthers|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402162509/http://www.panthers.at/Bundesliga/News/Kaderveraenderungen-bei-den-Panthers|url-status=dead|title=Kaderveraenderungen bei den Panthers|archive-date=April 2, 2015}} ==Coaching career== In 2012, Gaines was hired as an assistant coach at [[Bellarmine University]], where he coached for three seasons.{{Cite web |title=Bellarmine hires former Louisville basketball great Reece Gaines as assistant coach |url=http://www.courier-journal.com/article/20120829/SPORTS12/308290085/Bellarmine-hires-former-Louisville-basketball-great-Reece-Gaines-assistant-coach |url-status=dead}} While at Bellarmine, he helped the Knights to three straight [[NCAA Division II]] tournament appearances, including a Sweet 16 and a Final Four trip. In 2015, Gaines became an assistant coach at [[Eastern Kentucky University]].{{Cite web |title=Reece Gaines - Men's Basketball Coach |url=https://ekusports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/coaches/reece-gaines/794 |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=Eastern Kentucky University Athletics |language=en}} In 2018, Gaines was named acting coach after head coach [[Dan McHale]]'s contract was terminated.{{Cite web |last=Barker |first=Ricki |date=March 3, 2018 |title=EKU still owes McHale approximately $100,000 |url=https://www.richmondregister.com/sports/eku-still-owes-mchale-approximately/article_021790f6-1ea2-11e8-b133-fff1f73ede16.html |access-date=July 27, 2025 |website=richmondregister.com}} On November 5, 2019, the [[Austin Spurs]] announced that they had named Gaines as assistant coach.{{cite web |date=November 5, 2019 |title=AUSTIN SPURS ANNOUNCE 2019–20 COACHING STAFF ADDITIONS |url=https://austin.gleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-announce-2019-20-coaching-staff-additions/ |url-status=dead |access-date=November 5, 2019 |website=NBA.com |archive-date=August 10, 2022
